text: When you go out to war against your enemies and see horses and chariots and an army greater than your own, do not be afraid of them, for the LORD your God, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt, is with you.
When you are about to join battle, the priest shall come forward and speak to the troops.
He shall say to them: Hear, O Israel, today you are going into battle against your enemies. Do not lose heart. Do not be afraid, do not panic, and do not tremble before them,
for the LORD your God goes with you, to fight for you against your enemies and to save you.
Then the officers shall say to the troops: Is there a man who has built a new house and not yet dedicated it? Let him go back home, or he may die in the battle and another man dedicate it.
Is there a man who has planted a vineyard and not yet enjoyed its fruit? Let him go back home, or he may die in the battle and another man enjoy it.
Is there a man who is engaged to a woman and has not yet married her? Let him go back home, or he may die in the battle and another man marry her.
The officers shall speak to the troops again and say: Is there a man who is afraid and faint of heart? Let him go back home, so that he does not make his brothers' hearts melt like his own.
When the officers have finished speaking to the troops, they shall appoint army commanders at the head of the people.

versions.text: When the officers have finished speaking to the troops, they shall appoint commanders over the army to lead the people.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has 'commanders of armies at the head of the people.' The current rendering ('commanders over the army to lead the people') is slightly redundant and blurs the phrase בְּרֹאשׁ הָעָם ('at the head of the people'), which describes position in the marching order rather than a separate act of leading.

text: When you advance on a city to attack it, first offer it terms of peace.
If it accepts your offer of peace and opens its gates to you, then all the people found in it shall serve you as forced laborers.
But if it refuses peace and makes war against you, then lay siege to it.
When the LORD your God gives it into your hand, put every male in it to the sword.

But the women, the children, the livestock, and everything else in the city—all its spoil—you may take as plunder for yourself, and you may use the spoil of your enemies that the LORD your God has given you.
This is how you shall treat all the cities that lie very far from you, cities that are not among the cities of these nations.

versions.text: This is how you shall treat all the cities that lie far away from you, cities that do not belong to the nations here.
versions.explanation: The intensifier מְאֹד ('very far') is dropped, and 'the nations here' loses the demonstrative force of הַגּוֹיִם־הָאֵלֶּה ('these nations'), which points back to the Canaanite peoples named in verse 17.

text: But in the cities of these peoples that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, you shall leave nothing alive that breathes.
You shall devote them to destruction—the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites—just as the LORD your God has commanded you,
so that they may not teach you to imitate all the detestable things they do for their gods, and so you sin against the LORD your God.

When you besiege a city for a long time, waging war against it in order to capture it, do not destroy its trees by taking an axe to them; you may eat from them, but you shall not cut them down. Are the trees of the field human, that you should besiege them too?
Only trees that you know are not fruit trees may you destroy and cut down, to build siegeworks against the city that is waging war with you, until it falls.
